responses.content: The idea that humans only use a small percentage (like 10%) of their brain is a persistent myth. Modern neuroscience and brain imaging show that humans use virtually all parts of their brain, and different regions are active during various tasks. The entire brain is utilized, and the myth has been thoroughly debunked.
Humans use virtually all of their brain, with no specific percentage defined in scientific terms, as the 10% myth has been thoroughly debunked by neuroscience and brain imaging studies.

Humans use virtually all parts of their brain. There is no specific percentage defined in scientific terms, as the common claim that humans only use 10% of their brain is a thoroughly debunked myth. Modern neuroscience and brain imaging studies demonstrate that different brain regions are active during various tasks, indicating widespread utilization of the entire brain.
